channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77904-3

Induction of trained immunity can elicit anti-tumor effects. Here the authors show that histone deacetylase inhibitor preconditioning elicits a IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in monocytes/macrophages, promoting anti-tumor immunity in multiple triple negative breast cancer models.
item.dc:title: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages

item.title: Structural basis of laminin mimicry by E. coli CNF1 and its therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77975-2

The authors show how the bacterial toxin CNF1 mimics laminin to hijack its cell-surface receptor BCAM, and how this interaction can be repurposed to guide T cells to selectively kill BCAM-expressing cancer cells.
item.dc:title: Structural basis of laminin mimicry by E. coli CNF1 and its therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy

item.title: Microglial protein kinase CK2 prevents obesity in mice potentially through NLRP3 inflammasome activation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77895-1

The study demonstrates that microglial protein kinase CK2 prevents obesity in part via regulating food intake, potentially by regulating IL-18 production through ASC phosphorylation mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
item.dc:title: Microglial protein kinase CK2 prevents obesity in mice potentially through NLRP3 inflammasome activation

item.title: Stabilizing ruthenium atom layer neighbors through molecular and metal support interactions for water electrolyzers
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78037-3

Developing robust, low-noble metal catalysts is essential for practical anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis. Here, the authors use molecular and metal-support interactions to stabilize size-tuned ruthenium atom-layer neighbors, enabling efficient and durable hydrogen production.
item.dc:title: Stabilizing ruthenium atom layer neighbors through molecular and metal support interactions for water electrolyzers
